subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Titanium: Light, Strong, and Expensive
description: A quick win: understand Titanium: Light, Strong, and Expensive.

hook.text: Titanium is as strong as steel but 45% lighter. It also resists corrosion in seawater and acid.

buildup.text: The Kroll process extracts titanium using magnesium and chlorine gas at 800°C. It's slow and energy-intensive.

discovery.text: Jet engines use titanium because it keeps its strength at 600°C — where steel begins to weaken.

twist.text: The SR-71 Blackbird was 93% titanium. During the Cold War, the CIA bought it through fake companies from the Soviet Union.

climax.text: Medical implants use titanium because bone grows directly onto it. Your hip replacement might be titanium.

punchline.text: Strong as steel, light as aluminum, costs like gold.

quiz.question: Why is titanium used in jet engines?
options: It generates less noise than other metals at high speed
It maintains strength at 600°C where steel starts weakening
It is the only metal that can be shaped into fan blades
